# A Go importer calling a Go package that carries a `lang go` record
# must not wrap the call: passing nil crashes with the plain runtime
# error and no logos prefix [T-Sec5][R-U1].
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

cd w
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/gl.a ./gl/lib
go tool pack p $WORK/gl.a __.LOGOS
stdout '^logos-facts 3$'
stdout '^fn GoAssert AssertTP=1,AssertRTP=0$'
stdout '^lang go$'

logos build -o $WORK/bin/nilgo$GOEXE ./gc/cmd
! exec $WORK/bin/nilgo$GOEXE
! stderr 'logos: nil from Go value'
cd ..

-- w/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./gl
	./gc
)

-- w/gl/go.mod --
module example.com/gl

go 1.27

-- w/gl/lib/lib.go --
package lib

func GoAssert[T any](x any) T {
	return x.(T)
}

type User struct {
	Name string
}

func Get(u *User) string {
	return u.Name
}

-- w/gc/go.mod --
module example.com/gc

go 1.27

require example.com/gl v0.0.0

replace example.com/gl => ../gl

-- w/gc/q/q.go --
package q

import (
	"example.com/gl/lib"
	_ "logos/rt"
)

func DirectMsg() string {
	_ = lib.Get(nil)
	return "no-panic"
}

-- w/gc/cmd/main.go --
package main

import (
	"example.com/gc/q"
)

func main() {
	_ = q.DirectMsg()
}
